query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a significant content of Pt (around 50 at.%) to a single‐phase fcc FeCoNi alloy, followed by rapid thermal annealing (RTA), will induce L10 chemical ordering that dramatically increases magnetic anisotropy and thus raises the coercive field by orders of magnitude compared to the unmodified fcc alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy with low coercivity (<100 Oe)
generation.intervention: Introduce ~50 at.% Pt during alloy synthesis followed by rapid thermal annealing of the thin film
generation.conditions: Sputtered thin films deposited on thermally oxidized Si/SiO2 substrates at room temperature, subsequently subjected to a brief, high-temperature RTA process similar to that reported in prior studies
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of an L10 ordered intermetallic phase driven by Pt-induced chemical ordering
generation.mechanism: The Pt addition promotes long-range chemical ordering leading to the emergence of the L10 phase, which increases magnetic anisotropy through enhanced spin–orbit coupling and structural anisotropy. This augmented anisotropy impedes domain wall motion, thereby raising the coercive field significantly.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in coercivity by multiple orders of magnitude relative to the single-phase fcc FeCoNi, potentially shifting values from below 100 Oe to the kilooersted range under similar measurement conditions.
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi (or a matched derivative) exhibiting coercivity no greater than 100 Oe
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies to sputtered thin film samples on thermally oxidized Si/SiO2 substrates processed via RTA. Its validity in bulk samples or under different processing conditions is not currently supported.
generation.uncertainty: The precise coercivity magnitude increase depends on exact Pt content, annealing temperature/time, and film quality. Effects in bulk versus thin films remain to be explored.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of thin films: one with the baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi composition and another with ~50 at.% Pt added. Deposit both using identical sputtering conditions on thermally oxidized Si/SiO2 substrates. Subject both sets to an identical rapid thermal annealing process. Use X-ray diffraction (XRD) to verify the formation of the L10 phase in the Pt-doped films and employ magnetometry (e.g., VSM or SQUID) to measure coercivity.
measurements: Magnetometry (VSM or SQUID) for coercivity measurements
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Pt-added sample does not show clear evidence of L10 ordering and fails to exhibit a statistically significant increase (e.g., >10×) in coercivity compared to the single-phase fcc FeCoNi baseline, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractThe vast high entropy alloy (HEA) composition space is promising for discovery of new material phases with unique properties. This study explores the potential to achieve rare‐earth‐free high magnetic anisotropy materials in single‐phase HEA thin films. Thin films of FeCoNiMnCu sputtered on thermally oxidized Si/SiO2 substrates at room temperature are magnetically soft, with a coercivity on the order of 10 Oe. After post‐deposition rapid thermal annealing (RTA), the films exhibit a single face‐centered‐cubic phase, with an almost 40‐fold increase in coercivity. Inclusion of 50 at.% Pt in the film leads to ordering of a single L10 high entropy intermetallic phase after RTA, along with high magnetic anisotropy and 3 orders of magnitude coercivity increase. These results demonstrate a promising HEA approach to achieve high magnetic anisotropy materials using RTA.Keywords: high entropy alloy, magnetic anisotropy, rapid thermal annealing High entropy alloy (HEA) thin films are explored to achieve high magnetic anisotropy phases.
